items.stem: What is meant by "Unit cost"?
items.answer: The total cost of producing or buying and selling one unit of sale.

items.stem: Explain "Service business" with reference to the units of sale for different types of business.

items.stem: Kulkarni Industries, a bakery in Guwahati, makes two products. Chocolate cake: unit price ₹560, material ₹165, labour ₹65, overhead ₹65 per unit, monthly sales 550 units. Loaf of bread: unit price ₹190, material ₹45, labour ₹35, overhead ₹10 per unit, monthly sales 1,500 units. (a) Calculate the unit cost and unit margin of each product. (b) Calculate the total monthly margin from each. (c) Which product earns more per unit and which earns more in total? Why do the two answers differ?
items.answer: (a) Chocolate cake: unit cost ₹295, unit margin ₹265; loaf of bread: unit cost ₹90, unit margin ₹100. (b) Chocolate cake: ₹265 × 550 = ₹1,45,750; loaf of bread: ₹100 × 1,500 = ₹1,50,000. (c) The chocolate cake earns more per unit, but the loaf of bread earns more in total, because total margin = unit margin × number of units and the loaf of bread sells many more units.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 1 mark. (a) Chocolate cake: unit cost ₹295, unit margin ₹265; loaf of bread: unit cost ₹90, unit margin ₹100. (b) Chocolate cake: ₹265 × 550 = ₹1,45,750; loaf of bread: ₹100 × 1,500 = ₹1,50,000. (c) The chocolate cake earns more per unit, but the loaf of bread earns more in total, because total margin = unit margin × number of units and the loaf of bread sells many more units.

items.stem: Manish makes notebooks in Dehradun. Fixed costs are ₹1,19,14,000 per year; selling price ₹2,000 and variable cost ₹1,195 per notebook. Calculate the break-even point in units and in sales value.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for BEP in units, 1 mark for BEP in rupees. Contribution per notebook = ₹2,000 − ₹1,195 = ₹805. BEP = ₹1,19,14,000 ÷ ₹805 = 14,800 units; BEP sales = 14,800 × ₹2,000 = ₹2,96,00,000.

items.stem: Fatima plans to make cotton T-shirts. Fixed costs are ₹53,76,250 a year, the selling price is ₹1,205 and the variable cost is ₹630 per T-shirt. How many units must she sell to (a) break even and (b) earn a profit of ₹13,22,500? (c) What will be the sales value in (b)?

Malhotra and Sons, a small unit in Ranchi, makes notebooks. Selling price ₹1,455 per notebook; variable cost ₹780 per notebook; fixed costs ₹19,23,750 a year. It expects to sell 4,850 units this year. (a) Calculate the contribution per unit and the break-even point in units. (b) Calculate the margin of safety in units and the expected profit. (c) If rent raises fixed costs by ₹5,46,750, find the new break-even point and comment.
items.answer: (a) Contribution = ₹1,455 − ₹780 = ₹675; BEP = ₹19,23,750 ÷ ₹675 = 2,850 units. (b) MoS = 4,850 − 2,850 = 2,000 units; profit = MoS × contribution = 2,000 × ₹675 = ₹13,50,000. (c) New BEP = ₹24,70,500 ÷ ₹675 = 3,660 units; expected sales still exceed it, so the firm stays profitable but its margin of safety falls to 1,190 units.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 marks, (b) 2 marks, (c) 1 mark. (a) Contribution = ₹1,455 − ₹780 = ₹675; BEP = ₹19,23,750 ÷ ₹675 = 2,850 units. (b) MoS = 4,850 − 2,850 = 2,000 units; profit = MoS × contribution = 2,000 × ₹675 = ₹13,50,000. (c) New BEP = ₹24,70,500 ÷ ₹675 = 3,660 units; expected sales still exceed it, so the firm stays profitable but its margin of safety falls to 1,190 units.

items.stem: Khan Enterprises, a small unit in Kochi, makes water bottles. Selling price ₹155 per bottle; variable cost ₹115 per bottle; fixed costs ₹1,62,000 a year. It expects to sell 5,950 units this year. (a) Calculate the contribution per unit and the break-even point in units. (b) Calculate the margin of safety in units and the expected profit. (c) If rent raises fixed costs by ₹21,600, find the new break-even point and comment.
items.answer: (a) Contribution = ₹155 − ₹115 = ₹40; BEP = ₹1,62,000 ÷ ₹40 = 4,050 units. (b) MoS = 5,950 − 4,050 = 1,900 units; profit = MoS × contribution = 1,900 × ₹40 = ₹76,000. (c) New BEP = ₹1,83,600 ÷ ₹40 = 4,590 units; expected sales still exceed it, so the firm stays profitable but its margin of safety falls to 1,360 units.

items.stem: What is meant by "FIFO method"?
items.answer: A method of inventory valuation in which goods bought first are issued first, so closing stock is valued at the latest prices.

items.stem: Kabir runs Sethi Traders, a small manufacturing unit in Indore. (a) It uses 7,200 units of a component a year; ordering cost is ₹75 per order and carrying cost ₹3 per unit per year. Find the EOQ and the number of orders a year. (b) Its opening stock of finished goods was ₹99,000, closing stock ₹5,53,000 and cost of goods sold ₹32,60,000. Find the stock turnover ratio and the days stock is held (360-day year). (c) State what a low stock turnover would indicate.
items.answer: (a) EOQ = √(2 × 7,200 × 75 ÷ 3) = 600 units; orders = 7,200 ÷ 600 = 12. (b) Average inventory = ₹3,26,000; stock turnover = ₹32,60,000 ÷ ₹3,26,000 = 10 times; days = 360 ÷ 10 = 36 days. (c) A low ratio shows slow-moving or excess stock, which blocks working capital and raises carrying cost.

items.stem: Tanvi invested ₹41,50,000 in her printing business in Agra and earned a net profit of ₹8,30,000 this year. Calculate the return on investment and state what it shows.
items.answer: ROI = net profit ÷ investment × 100 = ₹8,30,000 ÷ ₹41,50,000 × 100 = 20%. It shows the profit earned on every ₹100 invested.

items.stem: For the year, Saxena Traders had sales of ₹68,30,000, cost of goods sold ₹34,70,000, operating expenses ₹7,45,000 and interest ₹95,000. Tax is 25% of profit before tax. Calculate (a) gross profit, (b) profit before tax and (c) net profit after tax.

Prepare a projected income statement of Chopra Brothers, Delhi, for its first year from: sales ₹67,10,000; cost of goods sold ₹46,60,000; salaries ₹1,58,000; rent ₹53,000; advertising ₹2,44,000; interest on loan ₹77,000; tax rate 25%. Also find the net profit as a percentage of sales.
items.answer: Sales ₹67,10,000 − cost of goods sold ₹46,60,000 = gross profit ₹20,50,000. Less operating expenses (salaries ₹1,58,000 + rent ₹53,000 + advertising ₹2,44,000 = ₹4,55,000) = operating profit ₹15,95,000. Less interest ₹77,000 = profit before tax ₹15,18,000. Less tax at 25% ₹3,79,500 = net profit ₹11,38,500. Net profit ratio = ₹11,38,500 ÷ ₹67,10,000 × 100 = 16.97%.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: gross profit, operating profit, profit before tax, net profit, net profit ratio. Sales ₹67,10,000 − cost of goods sold ₹46,60,000 = gross profit ₹20,50,000. Less operating expenses (salaries ₹1,58,000 + rent ₹53,000 + advertising ₹2,44,000 = ₹4,55,000) = operating profit ₹15,95,000. Less interest ₹77,000 = profit before tax ₹15,18,000. Less tax at 25% ₹3,79,500 = net profit ₹11,38,500. Net profit ratio = ₹11,38,500 ÷ ₹67,10,000 × 100 = 16.97%.

items.answer: (a) April: opening ₹1,00,000 + receipts ₹3,92,000 − payments ₹1,67,000 = closing ₹3,25,000. May: opening ₹3,25,000 + receipts ₹3,61,000 − payments ₹3,08,000 = closing ₹3,78,000. June: opening ₹3,78,000 + receipts ₹3,55,000 − payments ₹3,03,000 = closing ₹4,30,000. (b) No month has a cash shortage. (c) The surplus can be kept for emergencies, used to repay a loan or invested for a short period.
